'''Maurice Tubiana''' (25 March 1920 – 24 September 2013) was a French [[radiologist]], [[oncologist]], and researcher renowned for his contributions to cancer treatment and radiobiology.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Eschwege |first1=François |last2=Deutsch |first2=Eric |last3=Donaldson |first3=Sarah S. |date=March 2014 |title=Tribute to Professor Maurice Tubiana |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0360301613035827 |journal=International Journal of Radiation Oncology*Biology*Physics |language=en |volume=88 |issue=3 |pages=755–756 |doi=10.1016/j.ijrobp.2013.11.224|pmid=24521689 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was a key figure in advancing [[Radiation therapy|radiotherapy]] and cancer research in France during the 20th century.

== Early life and education ==
Born in [[Constantine, Algeria|Constantine]], [[French Algeria]] to a wealthy Jewish family, Tubiana joined the [[French Resistance]] during [[World War II]].<ref>{{Citation |last1=Schneider |first1=Maurice |chapter=Maurice Tubiana: The Fighting Spirit Behind Cancerology |date=2005 |title=European Oncology Leaders: The CancerFutures Collection 2001–2004 |pages=137–140 |editor-last=Veronesi |editor-first=Umberto |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-27069-8_16 |access-date=2024-08-29 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/3-540-27069-8_16 |isbn=978-3-540-27069-0 |last2=Brenner |first2=Raphaël |editor2-last=Redmond |editor2-first=Kathy|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> He obtained his medical degree in 1945 from the [[Académie Nationale de Médecine|National Academy of Medicine]] and later earned a doctorate in physics in 1947. Tubiana studied biophysics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1948 to 1949.

== Career and research ==
Tubiana pioneered the use of the [[betatron]] in cancer therapy, working with [[Frédéric Joliot-Curie]] to develop this technology.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dumancic |first1=Mirta |last2=Enger |first2=Shirin A. |date=August 2024 |title=Pioneering women in nuclear and radiation sciences |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0167814024006443 |journal=Radiotherapy and Oncology |language=en |volume=197 |article-number=110374 |doi=10.1016/j.radonc.2024.110374|pmid=38851301 |url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref> He led the first team to use computers for cancer treatment planning, marking a significant advancement in oncology.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-09-24 |title=Maurice Tubiana, médecin engagé |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/mon-figaro/2013/09/24/10001-20130924ARTFIG00660-maurice-tubiana-medecin-engage.php |access-date=2024-08-29 |website=Le Figaro |language=fr}}</ref>

From 1959 to 1982, Tubiana served as head of the radiation department at the [[Institut Gustave Roussy|Gustave Roussy Institute]] in [[Villejuif]]. He later became the institute's director from 1982 to 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History of Gustave Roussy – The Institute |url=https://www.gustaveroussy.fr/en/history-gustave-roussy-institute |access-date=2024-08-29 |website=Gustave Roussy |language=en}}</ref> Concurrently, he held the position of professor of experimental and clinical radiotherapy at the National Academy of Medicine in Paris from 1963 to 1989.

Tubiana authored over 300 scientific publications and several influential books, including "Introduction to Radiobiology," which became a standard text in the field.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Tubiana |first1=Maurice |title=Introduction to radiobiology |last2=Dutreix |first2=J. |last3=Wambersie |first3=A. |date=1990 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=978-0-85066-745-5 |location=London; New York}}</ref> He served as an expert consultant to the [[World Health Organization]] and the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Tribute to Maurice Tubiana 1920-2013 |url=https://www.iarc.who.int/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Maurice-Tubiana-IARC-web.pdf |work=[[World Health Organization]]}}</ref> and co-founded the [[European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology|European Society of Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology]], contributing to global health initiatives.

Beyond his research, Tubiana was a vocal advocate for public health. He championed anti-smoking campaigns and developed comprehensive public health plans addressing issues such as alcoholism and disease prevention.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tubiana |first=M. |date=January 1999 |title=Cancer Prevention |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/028418699432833 |journal=Acta Oncologica |language=en |volume=38 |issue=6 |pages=689–694 |doi=10.1080/028418699432833 |issn=0284-186X|url-access=subscription |doi-access=free }}</ref> From 1990 to 1993, he served as President of the High Council for Nuclear Safety and Information.

== Recognition and awards ==
Tubiana's contributions were widely recognized. He was elected to the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1988 and received numerous awards, including the Gray Medal (1981), the Breur Medal (1985), and the Röntgen Prize (1986).<ref name=":0" /> In 1993, he was awarded the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honor, France's highest order of merit.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biographie Maurice Tubiana Médecin, Universitaire, Membre de l´Institut |url=https://www.whoswho.fr/decede/biographie-maurice-tubiana_8849 |access-date=2024-08-29 |website=www.whoswho.fr}}</ref>
